items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Shots was with him a lot.

ctx.x: What about this bass with Ridgely when you were with it? Bass with Ridgely? Mm-hmm. Did he have one when you were with it?

Yeah, I'm not sure. Shots was with him a lot. Handy. Sills. David Jones. Mm-hmm. We played out the Suburban Garden. I was playing bass. Played out the Suburban Garden in 1928. Something else I wanted to ask you about.
Did they have many bands that had singers? Oh, no. Uh-huh. They wouldn't hire singers if they were out?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Shots, I knew him a pretty good while. But I really didn't know him well until he started playing music, you see.

ctx.x: How long did you know him?
Shots, I knew him a pretty good while. But I really didn't know him well until he started playing music, you see. Yeah. Mm-hmm.
Did you know Stink's brother Bill Johnson? No, I didn't know him.

Yeah, Raymond Brown. He would play. Then Handley, he would get on the drum, you know. Play a waltz, you know, until I come back. Yeah. Then after I left there in 29, around 20, yeah, I don't know, around 27, I played there about a year, 28. Celestine and Ridgely's band broke up then. That's when the band split. Well, I went with Ridgely. See, Ridgely made up a band. See, I went with Ridgely, paid with Ridgely down at Pete Hoyman's place. What do you call it? Planetation? Yeah. Planetation. That's right. I worked…
Shots, Handy, Sales. What did Handy play in those days? Alto and clarinet. Did he play much clarinet then? Oh, lots of clarinet. I can't think of this one. I'm a mic now.
About sales, how did he rate among the guitar players and banjo players?
